scope: Ordinary compatible-client/MCP attachment intake, MCP attachment toolkit and isolated nine-format document extraction. Complete protocol goal remains active.
implemented: Three MCP tools increase core catalog to34: prepare signed upload, caller-owned pending discard and send attachments through ordinary auto steering/queue admission.

Native thread or external request-namespace ownership survives transport reinitialization; ephemeral owner map expires staged entries on preparation and resets on restart. MCP grants do not require an ordinary owner session.

Nonpending MCP references must already exist in target messages; canonical stored metadata wins. Archived/unrelated/unauthorized targets reject; native sender and agent/MCP message/item origin survive active steering.

Shared claims copy/fsync pending files outside SQLite write locks across message dispatch, queued edits, question responses and staged launch. Rollback releases proven-unused copies, accepted receipt replay reuses durable identities after pending deletion.

100-attachment/80MiB image aggregate limits and image/file individual bounds precede copy. Duplicate ids reject. Future unknown descriptors preserve contract semantics. Context remapping changes only image/file attachment records.
Question references append quoted original/optional-extracted paths without changing string/array answer semantics; request and questionAnswer projections retain attachments and question text.
Rust worker supports docx/xlsx/pptx/odt/ods/odp/rtf/epub/ipynb, preserving source structure, cell normalization, format metadata, slide notes, notebook outputs, Unicode/code pages and HTML5 entities.

Worker:15s wall/CPU,256MiB address space,16MiB input,32MiB ZIP expansion,2048 entries,200k XML nodes/depth128,10k rows or notebook cells and512 columns,1million UTF16 output units and source truncation marker. No external retrieval or macro execution.

Per-State extraction serialization, immediate existing-sidecar reads, permanent invalid-input/1s transient failure caches, private atomic text sidecars. Parser failure retains original attachment. Embedded State exposes worker selection; binary selects itself.

Attachment-only provider bootstrap preserves stored user text and optional Ultrathink prefix. Both providers receive original/extracted file paths; previously queued file inputs can lazily obtain extraction outside DB lock.
